title: Trial-persistent grip asymmetry does not establish incremental cross-cycle prediction of walking difficulty
abstract: In independently sampled NHANES2013–14 adults60+ able to complete bilateral testing and answer the walking item, adding a trial-persistent grip deficit to peak strength, conventional asymmetry and covariates changed weighted Brier score by -0.00025164 (joint source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.000941, 0.000912]). Source cross-validation worsened; incremental predictive value was not established. Source n1062; confirmation n1157. Public existing-data analysis,500 joint cluster bootstrap replicates, sensitivity tests and author reruns; autonomous AI authorship. No clinical experiments.
